title: solo trip to Singapore
content:
I recently ventured to Singapore for the first time for about a week from 1/17 - 1/22! I actually started my journey on 1/15 but it took 2 days to get to Singapore >_<.

I took Etihad Airways for the first time from IAD <-> AUH <-> SIN. From IAD <-> AUH I flew a 787 and from AUH <-> SIN I flew an A380 for the first time!

Overall Etihad Airways was not bad at all - their IFE is nice and the service was fine. I liked how their seat headrests were bent on one side so it was easy to tilt your head when trying to rest without worrying about it going way off to the side lol. They also provided simple but useful amenity kits which included some hand cream and an eye mask.

Their catering was fine overall as well - it always seemed to be one main, one side, one dessert and one bread w/ butter. Interestingly, the dessert for each meal was almost always like some kind of mousse (which tasted good) but their side a couple times seemed overly peppery and a bit strange in flavor and texture overall (e.g. some kind of grain with bits of vegetables for example - healthy but not particularly flavorful and whatever flavor they tried to add didn't seem to work IMO). It would've been nice if they provided some kind of menu to know what the meals choices were and what they contained beforehand (the FAs would just tell us the options at ordering time).

Some airplane pics:


As for Singapore, I loved the weather! It was like a normal summer back home (east coast US) and I really lucked out with the weather - it only rained once and briefly when I was there! Most of the time it was sunny and cloudy-ish, with highs in the 80s I believe.

The food was great overall (although perhaps after you've been to a few hawker centers, the menu might appear a bit repetitive lol, e.g. Hainanese chicken everywhere) and inexpensive relative to what you might find in the US. I can't comment much on the prices for everything else but in general I don't think many things other than hawker food appeared to be significantly cheaper than what you'd see in the US.

Mandarin (and it sounds like Taiwanese Mandarin :D) is everywhere so plenty of opportunities for practice! One thing to note though is they do use simplified Chinese instead of traditional.

And everyone at least seems to know a bit of English so definitely helpful as well.

There were also a ton of malls to explore!


Changi Airport

The airport is definitely worth taking some time to explore, even just after arrival! I arrived in Terminal 2 I think but to see the famous Rain Vortex, you have to go to Changi Jewel, which is accessible in Terminal 1 (signage is easy to follow). There are walkways that connect Terminal 2 to Terminal 1 but on level 2 of Teminal 2 (look for an elevator, or 'lift' as they call it, to take you to L2, where there is a link bridge to JEWEL and skytrain to T1).

Throughout the airport was an abundance of shops and lots of little 'exhibits' of plants and water and fish!

Chinatown

My hotel was here and it's a fantastic location! Note the architecture, which is really interesting. It's super close to the Chinatown Complex Hawker Center, which is huge! And in the same building is a wet market on basement level. There is also an Indian temple in the area that attracts many worshippers.

It's also fairly close the Maxwell Hawker Center (where I had Hainanese chicken rice on my first day, which was quite good), Maxwell MRT station and the Buddha's Tooth Relic Temple. So much to see in the area!


The MRT is nice and clean, pretty much like Taiwan's. One super nice convenient thing that's not yet prevalent in other countries' MRTs as far as I know is that you can just use contactless payment via your Visa or Mastercard credit card to pay for train or bus fare! Really convenient.


Merlion spotted.

Pulau Ubin

A very nice island that is accessible by a bumboat ferry from Changi Village (it cost $4 SGD cash one way). I got to Changi Village via the 29 Bus at the bus terminal near Tampines MRT station. I saw a couple wild monkeys, a cool bird (Oriental Pied Hornbill I think) and loads of cool flora, including jackfruit trees and very large plants.


Singapore Botanic Gardens

Nice large area with lots of different kinds of plants divided into different sections.

There were also some river otters running around! :O


misc

I tried this interesting fruit for the first time called an attap seed. I quite liked it; it smelled like coconut and the flesh was jelly-like and sweet (kinda reminded me of lychee flesh).

There were so many expensive and exotic cars! Probably couldn't go a day without seeing a Bentley at least once and possibly even a Ferrari lol.

During the weekday I also heard and saw Singaporean air force fighter jets (F-16s and F-15s) flying around. This image was taken when I was at Gardens By The Bay. You could see F-15s and C-130s on approach to land at the airbase that's not too far away :D.

Other various foods I tried included kaya toast with peanut butter, chendol, nasi lemak and bak kut teh!

I got a Brunei $10 bill in change once and got worried but apparently Singapore and Brunei have a currency agreement such that their values are pretty much the same? Neat.
